newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRA claims responsibility for barracks blast.
newsitem.headline: IRA claims responsibility for barracks blast.

text.p: The Irish Republican Army claimed responsibility on Tuesday for the bombing of the British army's Norther Ireland headquarters in Lisburn.
The group made the claim in a call to Irish state radio, RTE, ending 24 hours of guesswork as to which group was reponsible for the worst attack in Northern Ireland in more than two years.
A telephone caller using a recognised password told the Dublin newsroom of RTE that its units had carried out the attack, which injured 31 people, 20 of them soldiers.
It said its target was British army personnel whom it accuses of propping up colonial rule of Northern Ireland.
The caller said injuries to civilans were regretted.
Earlier a caller to the same organisation claimed credit for the attack on behalf of the shadowy Irish Republican group, the Continuity Armed Council.

But that call was discounted by many Northern Ireland politicians because the caller did not use a recognised codewarod used to identify bona fide organisations wishing to broadcast bomb claims or warnings.
The IRA ended a 17-month ceasefire to its war against British rule in February this year but confined its bomb attacks to the British mainland and a British army base in Germany.
It had been widely accused of carrying out the Lisburn attack which breached the security of one of the most heavily fortified such bases in Western Europe.
The claim put intense pressure on a ceasefire by Protestant Loyalist gunmen who have stuck to their own two-year-old truce but warned it may crack if the IRA continues its campaign.
